clue.text: See 10
Homeric home edges away from using one vehicle

indicators.note: the outermost letters of the built phrase are cut away, its edges going

parts.note: with can mean using, as in 'cut with a knife'
one gives the article A
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An epic hero leaves home in a single vehicle, tiptoeing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges away from' strips the first and last letters off WITHACAR, leaving the island.
explanation.definitionFit: The island kingdom of Odysseus in Homer's Odyssey, to which he spends years trying to return.

clue.text: Being cruel to lecturer not unknown in 21 Down club

indicators.note: not before a word means that element is left out of what precedes

parts.note: bullying is being cruel to someone weaker
in algebra an unknown is x, y or z; here Y
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A student is cruel to a lecturer at a club in Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unknown' removes Y from BULLYING. The Bullingdon is an exclusive Oxford University dining club, famous for rowdy behaviour; David Cameron was a member.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusive, notoriously rowdy dining society for wealthy Oxford University students.

clue.text: Pork pies merchant, King and Queen seen after top class racing?

indicators.note: these pieces come after the racing element in the answer

parts.note: Formula One, F1, with the 1 written as I
BB King was the blues guitarist
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A trader in pork pies attends top motor racing with royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pork pies' is Cockney rhyming slang for lies, so a merchant in them tells them. 'King' is BB King, not R or K.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deals in lies, which rhyming slang calls pork pies, is a liar.

clue.text: Transport upturned in shifting dune that's not detected

indicators.note: one element sits inside the other
the letters of dune are shifted into a new order
in a down clue upturned reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: a cart is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A buggy overturns in moving sand dunes and vanishes without trace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturned' gives TRAC, which goes inside UNED, a mix of 'dune' from 'shifting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not found or tracked down remains without a trail being followed to it.

clue.text: Old American round piano gets musical work

indicators.note: the outer letters go round the inner one

parts.note: US, United States
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: An elderly American gathered round a piano produces a composition.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for work, used for a numbered composition in a composer's catalogue.

clue.text: Search occupies French dad with English ancestry

indicators.note: one word takes up space inside another

parts.note: pere is French for father
to dig is to search, as for information

explanation.surface: A search involving a French father turns up an English family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage or recorded descent, used of people and especially of animals.

clue.text: Star-shaped structure on point behind oarsmen?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece rests on another, so it comes first

parts.note: an aster is a star-shaped structure, as in a dividing cell
N, north, a compass point

explanation.surface: A star-shaped frame sits on a point behind a rowing crew.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition describes a position on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Towards or at the rear of a vessel, where a rowing crew's wake lies.

clue.text: Legendary heretic seizes day

indicators.note: one word grabs another and holds it inside

parts.note: an Arian followed Arius, condemned as heretical
Thur, short for Thursday

explanation.surface: A heretic grabs his day of fame and becomes the stuff of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to King Arthur and his knights, the stuff of British legend.

clue.text: Is TV personage abused in 14's alleged Pig Society?

definitions.note: the Oxford dining club named after the favourite of Edward II, in an allegation about David Cameron and a pig

indicators.note: the letters are mistreated and knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A TV personality is mistreated in a society linked to a former PM.
explanation.walkthrough: The Piers Gaveston Society is an Oxford dining club named after Edward II's favourite; a 2015 biography alleged a pig incident involving 14 there.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the society is that of Edward II's favourite, so it stands for the club.

clue.text: Tees is back to fill the Spanish post in computers

indicators.note: one element fills the inside of another

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: the setter Tees would say I am

explanation.surface: The setter returns to fill a post somewhere in IT.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Tees, so 'Tees is' is I AM; 'back' gives MAI, which fills EL.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail is correspondence, or post, sent between computers.

clue.text: Pig runs into her and bike's written off

indicators.note: one letter goes inside the others
a written-off bike is wrecked, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A pig charges into a woman and her bicycle is a write-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written off' mixes HER BIKES; R from 'runs' goes 'into' the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A black breed of domestic swine originating in the English county of that name.

clue.text: Coach or aircraft simulator

definitions.meaning: a sports coach, someone who trains
a flight ... is a simulator or training aircraft

explanation.surface: Choosing between a coach and a flight simulator.
explanation.definitionFit: One who coaches athletes; also a machine or plane used to teach pilots.

clue.text: Whipped cream covering Remainian leader

indicators.note: whipped cream is beaten, so its letters are churned

parts.note: on means covering, on top of

explanation.surface: Whipped cream tops something belonging to a Remain voter's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron led the Remain side in the 2016 Brexit referendum.
explanation.definitionFit: The prime minister who called and campaigned to stay in the EU referendum.

clue.text: Senegalese PM's mum upset by rude audio

indicators.note: the letters are upset and roughly jumbled together

parts.note: mum is an old form of address meaning madam, as in 'yes, mum'

explanation.surface: A prime minister's mother is offended by vulgar sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' gives MADAM, which joins AUDIO to be shuffled. Mamadou Dia was Senegal's first prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: He was Senegal's first head of government after independence in 1960.

clue.text: The Martian actor returns as The Wanderer

indicators.note: the name comes back, read from end to start

parts.note: Matt Damon starred in the film The Martian

explanation.surface: An actor from a sci-fi film comes back in a new film role.
explanation.definitionFit: One who roams from place to place with no fixed home.

clue.text: Animals moved to restrict current that powers ship

definitions.note: a clause standing for the noun it describes, a sail

indicators.note: the outer letters hold in another
the letters of the word are moved about

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Animals are moved aboard a ship, held back by the current.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal sail on a sailing vessel, the main source of its drive.

clue.text: Fit daughter requires assistance

parts.note: A1 means in top condition, written AI

explanation.surface: A healthy daughter still needs help.
explanation.definitionFit: Help or support given to someone who needs it.

clue.text: Sailor to err with the drink

parts.note: AB, able seaman
to sin is to err or transgress

explanation.surface: A sailor goes astray with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A potent green anise-flavoured spirit flavoured with wormwood.

clue.text: Convenes where pork, bacon and ham discussed?

indicators.note: talked about, so the word is heard spoken

parts.note: examples of meats

explanation.surface: A gathering where the talk is all of pork products.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathers together for a meeting or assembly.

clue.text: Reserved for special purpose or dismissed?

definitions.meaning: kept back for a particular use
a court can quash or annul a ruling

explanation.surface: Something held back or thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Held back for a specific use; also, of a judgment, annulled by a higher court.

clue.text: Gets bearings East and South

parts.note: the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: Someone finds their way using east and south.
explanation.definitionFit: Works out one's position or direction relative to surroundings.

clue.text: City's zero mark in vote for duke

parts.note: O looks like zero
a cross, X, is marked on a ballot

explanation.surface: A city records nothing on the ballot paper for its duke.
explanation.definitionFit: The English university city, home of 3 Down's club.

clue.text: Elderly notice Gloucestershire pig

parts.note: elderly means old
to spot is to notice

explanation.surface: An old person notices a West Country pig.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gloucestershire breed of pig is white with black spots; Gloucestershire is an English county.

clue.text: Much fluidity in early language made to move

parts.note: OE, Old English

indicators.note: the letters are made to move around

explanation.surface: An old tongue is made fluent and mobile.
explanation.definitionFit: Swelling caused by excess fluid collecting in body tissue.

clue.text: Sadness grips G&S in place of 12 or 22 Across

indicators.note: the outer word holds the inner letters inside

parts.note: pity is a feeling of sorrow
the letters G and S, as in Gilbert and Sullivan

explanation.surface: Pity takes hold of Gilbert and Sullivan in a pig's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 and 22 Across are both pig breeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen or shed where pigs are kept.

clue.text: Scoff about small Geordie town decorated with flowers

indicators.note: the outer word goes about the inner letters

parts.note: to scoff is to eat, feed
toon is the Newcastle (Geordie) pronunciation of town

explanation.surface: Eating around a small Newcastle town decked with blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a native of Newcastle upon Tyne, where 'town' is pronounced 'toon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hung with garlands or chains of blooms and ribbons.

clue.text: All right to stay at home for piggish remark

indicators.note: one element stays put inside the other

parts.note: OK means all right
in means at home

explanation.surface: Being told it's fine to stay home earns a grunt.
explanation.definitionFit: The grunting sound a pig makes.

clue.text: Eggs Burgess shelled

indicators.note: the word has its outside letters taken off, like an egg shelled

explanation.surface: Someone named Burgess is peeling eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eggs' is a verb, as in egging someone on.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg on is to encourage or press someone to act.

clue.text: Time as ruler — it's good to be in control

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: rein means control, as in keep a rein on

explanation.surface: A ruler says it's good to keep control.
explanation.definitionFit: The period during which a monarch sits on the throne.

clue.text: Clumsy punch cuts boxer Naz

indicators.note: one word cuts into another

parts.note: Prince Naseem (Naz) Hamed, British boxer
fist, to punch with the fist

explanation.surface: A punch opens a cut on a famous boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward and lacking skill with the hands.
